correctness.rationale: For an edge \(xy\), simultaneous adjacency is exactly membership in \(\langle x,yangle^\perp\). Nondegeneracy gives dimension \(n-r\), and only isotropic endpoints must then be removed, yielding the formula. The exceptional triangle-free boundary is obtained by a complete case split on \(r\), isotropy, \(n\), and \(q\); the absence of independent orthogonal isotropic pairs in dimension three follows from \(W\subseteq W^\perp\) contradicting dimensions. The rank-three counts follow from the exact \(q^2-1\) nonzero isotropic-vector count and degree sums. The embedded verifier exhaustively confirms representative prime and nonprime fields.

originality.rationale: The final claim was compared at the statement-and-implication level against the founding dot-product paper, the 2016 full finite-field treatment, the 2020 sequel, later domination work, own prior same-object findings, and the projective-polarity alias. The inspected same-object sources cover diameter/girth, vertex degrees, regularity, isomorphism rigidity, domination, and the two-dimensional component structure, but not the exact intersection of two endpoint neighborhoods in all dimensions. The rank-three polarity quotient is a real alias risk, so novelty is not assigned to the quotient itself; the accepted claim is the unprojectivized all-dimensional formula, scalar-dependent edge class, and sharp edge-triangle defect.
residual_risks: Finite-geometry literature uses several names for projective orthogonality graphs; an equivalent local count could exist under terminology not reached by the searches.

The rank-three quotient is classical, so originality is claimed for the all-dimensional unprojectivized edge formula and sharp defect boundary, not for the existence or basic properties of orthogonal polarity graphs.

value.rationale: The source literature already establishes girth three and vertex semiregularity, so the natural unresolved local question is how triangles distribute across edges. The theorem gives the complete answer from intrinsic endpoint data in every dimension, identifies the unique parameter pair with edges outside all triangles, and supplies an exact rank-three triangle count. This is structural information not recoverable from vertex degrees or global girth alone and is useful for local clustering, triangle enumeration, and comparisons with projective orthogonality graphs.
